evidence: Destination/days: article titled 'Things To Do in Segovia in 48 Hours'; 'Segovia is the perfect day trip from Madrid but I honestly don't think a day is enough. Instead I'd recommend spending a whole weekend here'; sections labeled Day 1 / Day 2.
Segovia Cathedral: 'the last Gothic cathedral built in Spain... From intricate Flemish tapestries to stunning marble statues' (L34-39).

La Almuzara: 'an artsy vegan-friendly cafe, tucked right next door to the Cathedral'; recommends 'guacamole with chips and the grapefruit and avocado salad'; 'Meson de Candid... is the go-to spot' for cochinillo (L45-56).

Alcazar of Segovia: 'a World Heritage Site... supposedly the inspiration behind Walt Disney's Cinderella Castle'; 'Hall of Kings... a frieze representing all of the Spanish rulers'; 'walk down to Mirador de la Pradera de San Marcos' (L62-72).
Church of Vera Cruz: 'Consecrated back in 1208, the church was built by the Knights Templar... probably the most unique because of its secluded location' (L78-85).

Casa de la Moneda Museum: 'will teach you about the history of money... view the machinery and tools used by the employees of the Spanish Royal Mint'; 'head to the nearby Jardines Del Rey... for a short walk' (L87-92).

Parador de Segovia: 'The hotel's terrace offers the best views of the city which are particularly magical at sunset... You can stop by for a full-on meal or just enjoy a glass of local red wine'; 'just 2 km (1.2 miles) of walking for the whole day' map (L98-105).

La Granja de San Ildefonso: 'hiring a car or ordering a taxi... lies in the hills near Segovia... Philip V modelled the palace on Versailles... the twenty-six fountains... the Baths of Diana are the real piece de resistance'; 'you can just walk around the gardens' without paying (L111-124).

La Huerta De San Lorenzo: 'a hidden gem of a restaurant called La Huerta De San Lorenzo'; 'Sustainably produced vegetables, farmed on site... Organic wine... you can even stay overnight in one of the upstairs bedrooms' (L129-139).

Aqueduct of Segovia: 'the stones aren't held together by mortar or cement. Oh, and it was in use until the mid-19th century... more than two thousand years old'; 'the Loba Capitolina, which sits right in front of it' (L145-155).

Jewish Quarter: 'Segovia's Jewish Quarter was once one of the richest communities in all of Castile'; 'the best preserved of its five synagogues is the former Main Synagogue which was converted into the Catholic Corpus Christi Convent' (L161-169).

El Fogon Sefardi: 'eating at El Fogon Sefardi. The restaurant's blend of traditional sephardic dishes and local Castilian influence'; alternative 'a touristy creperie with outdoor seating on Plaza del Azoguejo... to admire the aqueduct' (L175-182).
Madrid train: 'you can just fly to Madrid and then hop on the train for thirty minutes. It's that simple' (L23-25).
title: Things To Do in Segovia in 48 Hours

evidence: Destination: article titled '11 Things To Do In Menorca', Menorca Balearic Islands; numbered list of 11 items; no day-count claimed in packet (days null) - matches source.

Mahon: 'Menorca's capital... Sant Jaume Festival, which takes place on July 24-26... live music, fireworks and lots of horses'; 'try the local Xoriguer gin and pomada'; 'My favourite place to grab a drink was Bar Lemon' (L25-39).

Mahon Harbour + Isla del Lazareto: 'The best way to explore Mahon Harbour is by boat - my favourite were the glass-bottomed ones from a company called Yellow Catamarans'; 'catch a boat from Mahon Harbour to Isla del Lazareto... used as a quarantine... throughout the 19th century'; 'stick around until sunset' (L41-63).

Playa de Cavalleria: 'a natural beach on the north coast of Menorca... about a 10 minute walk from the nearest free car park. Don't forget to bring water and snacks, because there are no shops or restaurants here' (L65-74).

Binidali: 'It has crystal clear aquamarine waters... a beach bar with spectacular views perched on the rock above'; 'check out Cala Biniparratx... a limestone gorge with a sandy beach at the end, in a sheltered cove' (L79-87).

Ciutadella: 'Oh, Ciutadella! This was by far my favourite town on the island'; 'exploring the town's romantic side streets and the port'; 'don't forget to try an ensaimada, a traditional Mallorcan and Menorcan pastry'; 'The boutique hotels here are gorgeous' (L91-110).
Binibeca: 'This fishermen's village was designed by Spanish architect Antonio Sintes in 1972'; 'Those white facades and cobbled streets - it looks really authentic, right? Wrong!' (L114-121).
El Toro: 'El Toro is Menorca's tallest hill rising to a height of 342 m'; 'Atop the mountain you will find the Sanctuary of the Verge del Toro. There's also a towering statue of Christ' (L126-134).

S'Algar / Cala Alcaufar: 'S'Algar is a purpose built resort town... the nearby Cala Alcaufar beach is very peaceful, with just one bar and one restaurant. I especially loved the rock formations next to it. Head there to watch the sunset' (L136-144).

Binifadet Winery: 'You can enjoy a free guided tour of the winery, walk through the sun-drenched vineyards or savour a glass of wine on their vine-coverered porch... from soft sobrasada sausage to fish marinated in Xoriguer gin' (L146-154).
Cova d'en Xoroi: 'Cova d'en Xoroi is probably the coolest bar on the island - because where else can you enjoy a sundowner in a cave perched above the sea?' (L159-164).
title: 11 Things To Do In Menorca

evidence: Destination: article titled 'Travelling to Taiwan with Nataly & Murad Osmann'; all items direct quotes from the couple.
Toroko National Park: Nataly: 'I would recommend a visit to Toroko National Park... For the ultimate escape into an untouched environment that stands in complete contrast to buzzing Taipei' (L26-28).
Fo Guang temple: 'one of our favourite temples, Fo Guang, which is decorated by a huge statue of Buddha at its entrance' (L27-28).
Alishan region: Murad: 'we were quickly enchanted by the mountains and forests of the Alishan region, which truly looks like some sort of fairy-tale' (L32-34).

Emerald tea plantations and tea houses: 'We advise paying a visit to the emerald tea plantations which I'm sure would rival even the finest of those in India and Sri Lanka'; 'there are also tea houses, where you can take part in traditional tea ceremonies. We especially liked the ulun variety which was fragrant and subtle with a slightly spicy taste' (L44-49).
title: Taiwan travel recommendations (Nataly & Murad Osmann)

evidence: Title/destination: source profiles Lost Leblanc's 'How To Travel Bali – 14 Days in Paradise' video (L49); destination Bali supported throughout.

Days: source says the video is '14 Days in Paradise' but describes it as 'a 12-day itinerary for a trip to Bali, including a couple of days to get over the jet lag at the beginning' (L49-52). Packet's days=12 matches the source's '12-day itinerary' figure; the '14 Days' figure is the video title. Both figures originate in the source - no fabrication.

Canggu, Berawa Beach, Uluwatu, Ubud, Waterfalls, Adults-only resorts: 'Lost Leblanc mentions visiting Canggu, Berawa Beach, Uluwatu, and Ubud. He shares special highlights like waterfalls, tasty cuisine, and adults-only resorts' (L54-55).

Nusa Penida: 'Christian's number one recommendation when in Bali is to visit Nusa Penida, a hidden gem off the mainland. It's more expensive to visit because of its remoteness' (L65-69). Note: in the source this appears under his 'Top 10 Bali' video (2017), not the '14 Days' video - attribution looseness but it is a documented Lost Leblanc Bali recommendation.
title: How To Travel Bali – 14 Days in Paradise

evidence: Destination/days: 'The Ghorepani Poon Hill trek is a 4 – 5 day hike in the Annapurna mountain range in Nepal'; Day 1-5 itinerary structure; 'We did the Ghorepani Poon Hill trek in mid-March 2013' (L6-13).

Marigold Hotel (Amrit Tours): 'I stayed with, and booked everything through Marigold Hotel (Amrit Tours) - very highly recommended. The rooms at Marigold Hotel are around 700 Rupees'; 'we arranged our guide from Marigold Hotel (Amrit Tours) in Pokhara, at a cost of $20 US per day. We hired a guide for 5 days (so $100 for our guide)' (L159-198).
Taxi Pokhara to Nayapul: 'Starting at about 8 am from Pokhara... we took a taxi (taxi cost us 1,500 Nepali Rupees) to Nayapul'; 'Total trekking time - about 5-6 hours' (L20-41).

Green Land Restaurant: 'We stopped for lunch at Green Land Restaurant, a small house restaurant... I chose vegetarian dal bhat for lunch... they offered as much rice as I could eat for 300 Rupees' (L25-27).

Tikhedunga Guest House: 'checked into Tikhedunga Guest House... Our double room cost just 350 Rupees'; 'I ordered a plate of white plain rice (150 Rupees), and a plate of stir fried veg noodles (270 Rupees)... a cup of tea (50 Rupees)' (L31-35).

Hike Tikhedunga to Ghorepani: 'we walked straight up the face of the mountain for about 4 hours, eventually catching glimpses of the white snow capped Annapurna peaks'; lunch 'sukuti (dry buffalo)... she fried it up with some onions and spices... all I could eat for 400 Rupees'; 'Total hiking hours - about 7-8 hours' (L50-70).

Dhaulagiri Lodge: 'checked in to Dhaulagiri Lodge, located right at the top of the village in the main square area. They charged 300 Rupees for our room and 100 Rupees for a hot shower'; dinner 'vegetable fried rice (260 Rupees) and a cup of milk tea (60 Rupees)' (L61-68).

Sunrise at Poon Hill summit: 'At 5 am... made the 45 minute climb to the top of Poon Hill for sunrise'; intro: 'At 3,210 meters, the Poon Hill sunrise view of the snowy rugged Annapurna Himalaya range'; 'hiked along a parallel ridge... until arriving in... Gandruk'; lunch 'vegetarian dal bhat... Price for dal bhat was 360 Rupees'; 'Total hiking hours - about 10-12 hours' (L2, L78-104).
Muna Hotel: 'We stayed at Muna Hotel for 350 Rupees per night' in Gandruk (L100).

Hike Gandruk to Deurali: 'I ordered up a huge plate of... dal baht (360 Rupees) for breakfast'; 'The trail was mostly downhill, and mostly stone steps... passing through small villages and numerous small farms'; 'Total hiking time - about 10 hours' (L110-129).
Hotel Trekkers Inn: 'We got a room at Hotel Trekkers Inn (350 Rupees)... cooked us some delicious Tibet bread (140 Rupees) and an omelet with rice (320 Rupees)' in Deurali (L124-125).

Hike Deurali to Pothana, taxi to Pokhara: 'It only took about an hour to reach the permit check town of Pothana... arranged plans from Marigold Hotel... for our guide to lead us to the Annapurna Eco Village (1,000 Rupees per night)... stayed for just 1 night before catching a taxi back to civilization, Pokhara' (L133-143).
title: Ghorepani Poon Hill Trek - Ultimate Guide and Itinerary

evidence: Destination/days: 'Kara and I just completed our 11 day Trans-Siberian journey from Moscow to Vladivostok. Our entire journey covered over 9,280 km'; 'Our trip lasted 10 days and 11 nights. Four days were spent on land and 6 days were spent on the train' (L4-6, L197-204). Packet days=11 matches.

Trans-Siberian train Moscow to Irkutsk: 'The first leg of our trip was from Moscow to Irkutsk. This was 74 hours of non-stop train travel' (L197). Source also covers visas, ticket buying, train classes throughout.

Irkutsk - Lake Baikal: 'We stopped in Irkutsk for two nights'; 'The main draw of this stop is seeing Lake Baikal, which is the deepest lake in the world... a popular island on the lake called Olkhon Island... you need at least 3 days for this trip. It takes 7 hours by the time you drive to the lake and ferry to the island' (L199, L221-228).
Train Irkutsk to Ulan-Ude: 'Then we hopped back on the train for a short 6.5 hour ride to our second stop of Ulan-Ude' (L199).

Ulan-Ude sightseeing: 'We stayed in Ulan-Ude for two nights'; 'Ulan-Ude, on the other hand, could definitely be seen in a day'; attractions: 'the world's largest statue of Lenin's head, the main walking street in the center of town, a beautiful church that sits near the end of the walking street, a monastery that sits on a hill and overlooks the city, and another monastery that's located 45 minutes outside of the city' (L199-233).

Train Ulan-Ude to Vladivostok: 'the final leg of our journey to Vladivostok which was another 64 hours of non-stop train travel'; 'I didn't come across much to do between Ulan-Ude and Vladivostok' (L201, L238-239).

Vladivostok stopover: 'completed our 11 day Trans-Siberian journey from Moscow to Vladivostok'; 'The last change I would have made on our journey would be the amount of time we spent in Vladivostok. Unfortunately, the flight we needed to get to our next...' (L4, L241).

Russian visa logistics: 'There are actually three steps in the visa process: 1. You need to get a letter of invitation. 2. You need to get a visa. 3. You need to register your visa'; 'we used VisaHQ to obtain our visa... they were going to charge us $50 per person for a letter of invitation'; 'Fortuna Travel offered letters of invitation for only $12' (L66-90).

Suggested stops Kazan and Yekaterinburg: 'They all recommended that we stop in the town of Kazan. It's a predominately Muslim city'; 'you'll want to stop at Yekaterinburg. It's the town where the last tsar of Russia and his family were executed' (L210-219).
title: The Ultimate Guide to Riding the Trans-Siberian Railway (Moscow to Vladivostok)

evidence: Destination: article titled 'Visit Borneo: Guide by Photographer Emmett Sparling'; 'Find out where to eat, where to go and what to do in Derawan Islands, Borneo' (L0-2). No day count claimed (days null).
Boat from Tarakan: 'Getting There: 5-hour boat ride from Tarakan' (L8-10).
Derawan Island homestay: 'Derawan Island in a homestay. There are about six homestays to choose from and they're all huts on stilts over the water' (L4-6).
Warungs: 'There are a few basic restaurants called Warung's. Warungs are like an Indonesian version of a Subway... They serve traditional Indonesian food for lunch and dinner' (L16-19).
Jellyfish Lake: 'Jellyfish Lake in Kakaban Island. 2-4 hour speed boat ride from Derawan. It's filled with millions of harmless jellyfish. You can swim in there' (L21-24).
Snorkelling / free diving: 'Snorkelling or free diving. There are lots of beautiful places to choose, from the Jellyfish Lake to the underwater forest' (L26-28).
Bike around Derawan: 'On Derawan, you can rent bikes and bike around the island... You can bike around the whole island in about 30 minutes' (L30-31).

Light-beam canyon: 'There's a canyon where at certain times of day, light beams shine through the opening. It's really beautiful. If you ask a local about it they'll tell you how to reach it' (L37-40).
title: Visit Borneo: Derawan Islands guide by Emmett Sparling
